brief:
Swedish voters head to the polls as the left-wing coalition leads in surveys, positioning Israel and Palestine policies as central campaign issues. The current right-wing government's stance on these matters faces potential scrutiny if opposition parties gain power, Al Jazeera English reported. Political parties across the spectrum have staked out distinct positions on recognizing Palestinian statehood and relations with Israel.

The election timing coincides with intensified debate across Europe over Middle East diplomacy. A shift in government could reshape Sweden's approach to the conflict, affecting the country's voting patterns at the United Nations and its diplomatic engagement with both Israeli and Palestinian authorities. The outcome will determine which policies guide Swedish foreign policy in the region over the coming years.
dek: With the left-wing coalition ahead in polling, the current right-wing government's policies could soon be up for debate.
title: Sweden's election puts Israel-Palestine policies on trial
